Hi Dana — following up with the operational details Ben promised. I've included a short, answer-oriented Q&A below and attached a deletion flow diagram.

1) Physical residency
   - Tenant data (requests, outputs, model KV cache associated with tenant) is stored in the customer-selected cloud region. We host buckets, snapshots, and transient storage in the same region by default.

2) Default retention windows (configurable at account level)
   - Request & access logs: 90 days (configurable down to 30 days for enterprise accounts).
   - Short-term KV/cache: default 7 days for conversation context; we provide APIs to reduce TTL to zero for stricter retention.
   - Backups / snapshots: rolling snapshots are retained for 30 days by default. Snapshots are immutable once created and follow the snapshot lifecycle described in the attachment.

3) Deletion process & timelines
   - Deletion request (API or support): 0-24 hours to acknowledge.
   - Primary storage purge: initiation within 48 hours; deletion operations target all primary object stores and tenant-specific indexes.
   - Replica removal: cross-region replicas (if enabled) are removed as part of the purge; removal completes within 48-72 hours depending on replication state.
   - Backup snapshot purging: snapshots are queued for deletion and removed per the snapshot lifecycle (typically completed within 30 days from purge request).
   - Finalization & evidence: we generate an audit package (object delete logs, purge job ids, and verification checksums) and can issue a deletion confirmation/certificate within 5 business days.

4) Backups and cross-region replication
   - By default, we do not enable cross-region replication for hosted API tenants unless explicitly requested. For customers that require cross-region replication we maintain configuration flags and can limit replication to a single geopolitical group (e.g., EU-only).

5) Runtime logs & PII
   - Application-level logs are redacted by default. Raw request payloads are not stored in plaintext logs. Sensitive fields (SSNs, credit card numbers, large free-text PII) are redacted during ingestion where possible; customers can supply field-masking rules via the Console to extend redaction.

6) Evidence & auditability
   - We can provide: deletion confirmation PDF, audit export (S3 object deletion events), and an engineer-signed verification note. SOC 2 summary available; full report shared under NDA.

See attached: hostedapi-deletion-flow.png (process flow); data-retention-playbook.pdf (timeline + config options).

Alex — quick answers to your bullets, and next steps below.

- Backup location: Backups are stored in the same cloud provider as the primary data (we don’t copy backups to a secondary cloud provider unless explicitly configured in an integration). When EU-only is selected we keep backups within the EU cloud region and do not replicate to US by default.

- Edge telemetry & observability: All control-plane telemetry is instrumented for operational health but does not contain tenant payloads. For EU-only tenants we can opt into region-restricted telemetry (no TTLs or aggregated metrics leave the EU); our Console supports region restriction for observability when required.

- Shorten backup purge to 7 days: Technically possible for enterprise accounts with reserved configuration. Constraints are around snapshot immutability and retention windows enforced by our snapshot pipeline (we enforce a minimum 7-day quiesce period for snapshots to ensure restore capability). We can make 7 days the minimum for backups with an enterprise contract amendment.

- Deletion certificate: Yes — we provide a signed deletion confirmation that includes deletion job ids, S3 object ids (or provider equivalents), and deletion timestamps. We can deliver this as a PDF signed by our Security PM within 5 business days of completion.
